newsitem.title: POLAND: Two Polish soccer stadiums closed after violence.
newsitem.headline: Two Polish soccer stadiums closed after violence.

text.p: The governor of Warsaw on Monday ordered the closure of two stadiums in the Polish capital after weekend violence by soccer hooligans.

"Warsaw Governor Bohdan Jastrzebski on Monday issued an order banning matches at the stadiums of Polonia and Legia until those clubs can ensure the safe organisation of matches," PAP quoted the governor's office as saying.

At Saturday's match between Warsaw's two first-division teams at Polonia Stadium, hordes of drunken hooligans clashed with police, set fire to the club's buildings and then rampaged through the streets smashing windows and damaging cars.
Thirty-seven policemen were injured, three seriously.
Police detained 76 of the worst trouble-makers, misdemeanours courts fined several of them and others are due to face trial on criminal charges.
Following a wave of growing youth violence, the incident has captured the attention of Poland's top political leaders.

President Aleksander Kwasniewski, a former sports minister, on Monday conferred on the matter with the interior minister and defence minister. The government is expected to discuss the issue at Tuesday's weekly cabinet meeting.
Police said on public television that some 1,000 instances of stadium violence occurred in Poland last year, and a 40,000-strong group of hard-core hooligans were largely to blame.
